title: The Three Signals
story: An encrypted vault flickers to life and shows three signals.
instructions: Use every clue. Single-digit answers inside a pair need a leading zero (6 becomes 06). Enter the six-digit code.

clues.text: First pair: the number of sides on a hexagon, followed by the number of sides on a square.
Middle pair: the smallest two-digit prime number.
Last pair: the number of hours on a clock face, minus six.

explanation: A hexagon has 6 sides and a square has 4, so the first pair is 64. The smallest two-digit prime is 11. 12 - 6 = 6, written as 06. The code is 641106.
steps: A hexagon has 6 sides and a square has 4, so the first pair is 64.
hints: Each clue describes one pair of digits, left to right.
A hexagon has 6 sides and a square has 4. A clock face shows 12 hours. A single digit such as 6 is written 06.
Near the end: the code starts with 64 and ends with 6. Work out the middle three digits yourself.

title: Seven Steps
story: A counter on the wall freezes mid-count.
instructions: Use every clue. Single-digit answers inside a pair need a leading zero (6 becomes 06). Enter the six-digit code.

clues.text: The panel shows 7, 14, 21, 28. The code is the next three terms written as three pairs.

explanation: The sequence rises by 7 each step. The next three terms are 35, 42 and 49. The code is 354249.
steps: The sequence rises by 7 each step.
The next three terms are 35, 42 and 49.
hints: What is added each time?
The sequence rises by 7. Continue it three more times and write each term as a pair.
Near the end: the code starts with 35 and ends with 9. Work out the middle three digits yourself.

title: Odd One Out
story: Five numbered tiles hang on the door. One does not belong.
instructions: Use every clue. Single-digit answers inside a pair need a leading zero (6 becomes 06). Enter the six-digit code.

clues.text: Tiles: 16, 25, 36, 52, 49. The first pair is the tile that does not belong.
The middle pair is the digit sum of that tile, written with two digits.
The last pair is the number of tiles.

explanation: Perfect squares: 16, 25, 36, 49. 52 is not a square. Digit sum of 52 is 7, written 07. There are 5 tiles, written 05. The code is 520705.
steps: Perfect squares: 16, 25, 36, 49. 52 is not a square.
hints: Four tiles share a property. Which one breaks it?
Four of the tiles are perfect squares. Add the two digits of the odd tile, then count all the tiles.
Near the end: the code starts with 52 and ends with 5. Work out the middle three digits yourself.

title: Matching Pairs
story: Three identical keypads sit side by side.
instructions: Use every clue. Single-digit answers inside a pair need a leading zero (6 becomes 06). Enter the six-digit code.

clues.text: The three pairs of digits are identical.
All six digits add up to 18.
The first digit is two more than the second digit.

explanation: The code looks like ababab, so 3 x (a + b) = 18 and a + b = 6. Also a = b + 2, so b = 2 and a = 4. The code is 424242. The code is 424242.
steps: The code looks like ababab, so 3 x (a + b) = 18 and a + b = 6.
Also a = b + 2, so b = 2 and a = 4.
hints: If every pair is the same, you only need to find one pair.
Call the pair "ab". Then three times (a + b) is 18.
Near the end: the code starts with 42 and ends with 2. Work out the middle three digits yourself.

title: Shape Census
story: Rows of glowing glyphs scroll across the panel.
instructions: Use every clue. Single-digit answers inside a pair need a leading zero (6 becomes 06). Enter the six-digit code.

clues.text: The first pair is the number of triangles (▲).
The middle pair is the number of squares (■).
The last pair is the number of circles (●).

explanation: Triangles: 7, squares: 5, circles: 4. The code is 070504.
hints: Count one kind of shape at a time.
Go row by row and keep a running total for each shape. Write single-digit totals with a leading zero.
Near the end: the code starts with 07 and ends with 4. Work out the middle three digits yourself.

title: Three Riddles
story: The vault asks three questions before it will listen.
instructions: Use every clue. Single-digit answers inside a pair need a leading zero (6 becomes 06). Enter the six-digit code.

clues.text: First pair: "I have an extra day only every four years. How many days am I in February then?"
Middle pair: "How many letters are in the word VAULT?"
Last pair: "How many colours are in a rainbow?"

explanation: 29 days in a leap-year February. V-A-U-L-T has 5 letters: 05. A rainbow has 7 colours: 07. The code is 290507.
hints: These are three small facts, one per pair.
A leap-year February has 29 days. VAULT has 5 letters, so write 05.
Near the end: the code starts with 29 and ends with 7. Work out the middle three digits yourself.

title: Up Three, Down One
story: The keypad lights flash in a strange rhythm.
instructions: Use every clue. Single-digit answers inside a pair need a leading zero (6 becomes 06). Enter the six-digit code.

clues.text: The first digit is the number of wheels on a bicycle.
Each later digit is 3 more than the digit before it, then 1 less, then 3 more, alternating (+3, -1, +3, -1, +3).

explanation: A bicycle has 2 wheels. 2, 5, 4, 7, 6, 9. The code is 254769.
hints: Find the first digit, then follow the rule.
Start at 2. Add 3, subtract 1, and keep alternating for five steps.
Near the end: the code starts with 25 and ends with 9. Work out the middle three digits yourself.

title: The Mirror Lock
story: The lock reads the same in its own reflection.
instructions: Use every clue. Single-digit answers inside a pair need a leading zero (6 becomes 06). Enter the six-digit code.

clues.text: The code reads the same forwards and backwards.
The digits add up to 22.
The first digit is even and the second digit is one more than the first.
The third digit is half of the first digit.

explanation: Call the first digit a. Then the second is a + 1 and the third is a / 2. a + (a + 1) + a/2 = 11, so a = 4. The first three digits are 4, 5, 2, mirrored: 452254. The code is 452254.
steps: Call the first digit a. Then the second is a + 1 and the third is a / 2.
The first three digits are 4, 5, 2, mirrored: 452254.
hints: A palindrome of six digits is determined by its first three digits.
The digit sum is twice (first + second + third), so those three add up to 11.
Near the end: the code starts with 45 and ends with 4. Work out the middle three digits yourself.

title: Cube Facts
story: A glowing cube spins in the centre of the vault.
instructions: Use every clue. Single-digit answers inside a pair need a leading zero (6 becomes 06). Enter the six-digit code.

clues.text: First pair: the number of faces on a cube.
Middle pair: the number of edges on a cube.
Last pair: the number of vertices on a cube.

explanation: 6 faces, 12 edges, 8 vertices. Code: 06 12 08. The code is 061208.
hints: Picture a die.
A die has 6 faces, 12 edges and 8 corners. Write 6 and 8 with leading zeros.
Near the end: the code starts with 06 and ends with 8. Work out the middle three digits yourself.

title: The Missing Numbers
story: A 3 x 3 grid of numbers has two scratched-out cells.
instructions: Use every clue. Single-digit answers inside a pair need a leading zero (6 becomes 06). Enter the six-digit code.

clues.text: Every row, column and diagonal of the grid adds up to the same total.
First pair: the number in the cell marked A, then the number in the cell marked B.
Middle pair: the shared total of each row.
Last pair: the centre number, then the bottom-left number.

explanation: The bottom row 4 + 9 + 2 gives the total 15. Row 1: 8 + A + 6 = 15 so A = 1. Row 2: 3 + 5 + B = 15 so B = 7. Pairs: 17, 15, 54. The code is 171554.
steps: The bottom row 4 + 9 + 2 gives the total 15.
hints: Use a complete row to find the shared total first.
The bottom row 4 + 9 + 2 already tells you the shared total.
Near the end: the code starts with 17 and ends with 4. Work out the middle three digits yourself.

title: Fibonacci Fragment
story: A torn note shows the start of a famous sequence.
instructions: Use every clue. Single-digit answers inside a pair need a leading zero (6 becomes 06). Enter the six-digit code.

clues.text: The note reads 2, 3, 5, 8, 13, 21. The code is the next three terms as pairs.

hints: Look at how 5 relates to 2 and 3.
Each term is the sum of the two before it.
Near the end: the code starts with 34 and ends with 9. Work out the middle three digits yourself.

title: Pocket Change
story: A tray of coins sits beside the lock: 4 quarters, 3 dimes, 2 nickels and 7 pennies.
instructions: Use every clue. Single-digit answers inside a pair need a leading zero (6 becomes 06). Enter the six-digit code.

clues.text: First pair: the total number of coins.
Middle pair: the total value in cents, minus 100.
Last pair: the number of dimes and nickels together.

explanation: 16 coins in all. 147 - 100 = 47. Dimes plus nickels: 3 + 2 = 5, written 05. The code is 164705.
hints: Quarters are 25, dimes 10, nickels 5, pennies 1 cent.
Total value is 100 + 30 + 10 + 7 = 147 cents.
Near the end: the code starts with 16 and ends with 5. Work out the middle three digits yourself.

title: Letter Count
story: The vault password hint is a single long word: ENCRYPTION.
instructions: Use every clue. Single-digit answers inside a pair need a leading zero (6 becomes 06). Enter the six-digit code.

clues.text: First pair: the number of letters in ENCRYPTION.
Middle pair: the number of vowels (A, E, I, O, U) in it.
Last pair: the alphabet position of its first letter.

explanation: 10 letters. Vowels E, I, O: 03. E = 5: 05. The code is 100305.
hints: Spell the word out and tick off letters.
The vowels are E, I and O. E is the fifth letter of the alphabet.
Near the end: the code starts with 10 and ends with 5. Work out the middle three digits yourself.

title: Ana and Ben
story: Two names are carved into the door with an age riddle.
instructions: Use every clue. Single-digit answers inside a pair need a leading zero (6 becomes 06). Enter the six-digit code.

clues.text: Ana is three times as old as Ben.
In six years Ana will be exactly twice as old as Ben.
The code is Ana's age now, Ben's age now, then the sum of their ages in six years.

explanation: 3b + 6 = 2b + 12 gives b = 6 and Ana = 18. In six years: 24 + 12 = 36. Code: 18 06 36. The code is 180636.
hints: Let Ben be b years old. Write Ana in terms of b.
Solve 3b + 6 = 2(b + 6).
Near the end: the code starts with 18 and ends with 6. Work out the middle three digits yourself.

title: Elevator Log
story: The vault elevator starts at floor 0. Its log lists moves: up 7, down 3, up 12, down 5, up 4.
instructions: Use every clue. Single-digit answers inside a pair need a leading zero (6 becomes 06). Enter the six-digit code.

clues.text: First pair: the floor where the elevator ends.
Middle pair: the total number of floors travelled.
Last pair: the highest floor it reached.

explanation: Final floor 15. Total distance 31. Highest floor 16. The code is 153116.
hints: Track the floor after every move.
Floors: 7, 4, 16, 11, 15. Distance ignores direction.
Near the end: the code starts with 15 and ends with 6. Work out the middle three digits yourself.

title: Twin Sets
story: Three pairs of digits must be arranged along six slots.
instructions: Use every clue. Single-digit answers inside a pair need a leading zero (6 becomes 06). Enter the six-digit code.

clues.text: The code uses the digits 1, 1, 2, 2, 3, 3 exactly once each.
No two equal digits are next to each other.
The code starts with 1 and ends with 2.
The two 3s are exactly three places apart.
The two 1s are exactly two places apart.

explanation: Positions 1 and 6 are taken, so the 3s must be in positions 2 and 5. The remaining 1 and 2 go in positions 3 and 4. The 1s are two apart, so 1 is in position 3. Code: 1 3 1 2 3 2. The code is 131232.
steps: Positions 1 and 6 are taken, so the 3s must be in positions 2 and 5.
The remaining 1 and 2 go in positions 3 and 4. The 1s are two apart, so 1 is in position 3.
hints: Place the fixed digits first: 1 at the start, 2 at the end.
Which positions can two 3s occupy if they are three apart and the ends are taken?
Near the end: the code starts with 13 and ends with 2. Work out the middle three digits yourself.

title: Dice Tower
story: Three dice are stacked on the vault ledge.
instructions: Use every clue. Single-digit answers inside a pair need a leading zero (6 becomes 06). Enter the six-digit code.

clues.text: The tops of the three dice show 2, 5 and 3. On a die, opposite faces always add up to 7.
The code is the three top faces, then the three hidden bottom faces of the same dice in the same order.

explanation: Bottoms: 5, 2, 4. Code: 253524. The code is 253524.
hints: Which number is opposite 2?
Bottom = 7 minus top for each die.
Near the end: the code starts with 25 and ends with 4. Work out the middle three digits yourself.

clues.text: The first three digits are the odd numbers in the order they appear.
The last three digits are the even numbers in reverse order of appearance.

explanation: Odds in order: 5, 3, 1. Evens reversed: 4, 6, 8. Code: 531468. The code is 531468.
hints: Split the belt into odd and even numbers.
Odds keep their order; evens are reversed.
Near the end: the code starts with 53 and ends with 8. Work out the middle three digits yourself.

title: Quick Sums

instructions: Use every clue. Single-digit answers inside a pair need a leading zero (6 becomes 06). Enter the six-digit code.

clues.text: First pair: 7 x 8.
Middle pair: 100 - 37.
Last pair: 3 x 3, written with two digits.

explanation: 56, 63 and 09. The code is 566309.
hints: Three small calculations.
Single-digit answers need a leading zero.
Near the end: the code starts with 56 and ends with 9. Work out the middle three digits yourself.

title: The Gatekeeper
story: The first chapter ends with a guard who only speaks in rules.
instructions: Use every clue. Single-digit answers inside a pair need a leading zero (6 becomes 06). Enter the six-digit code.

clues.text: The first digit is the number of sides on a triangle.
The second digit is the number of wheels on a unicycle.
Every later digit is the last digit of the sum of the two digits before it.

explanation: 3 and 1 start the code. 3+1=4, 1+4=5, 4+5=9, 5+9=14 so 4. Code: 314594. The code is 314594.
hints: The first two digits come from facts, the rest from a rule.
The rule is like Fibonacci but only the last digit is kept.
Near the end: the code starts with 31 and ends with 4. Work out the middle three digits yourself.
